title: Lanthanide-Titanium Oxo Clusters as the Luminescence Sensor for Nitrobenzene Detection

synthesis.procedure: Europium(III) acetate hydrate, 4-tert-butylbenzoic acid, and 1,10-phenanthroline monohydrate were dissolved in acetonitrile in a Pyrex vial. Titanium tetraisopropanolate was added, and the mixture was sonicated for 10 min, then heated at 80 °C for 1 day. After cooling to room temperature, colorless crystals of 1 were obtained.
synthesis.time: Sonication for 10 min; heating for 1 day
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Pyrex vial; sonication followed by oven heating
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooled to room temperature to obtain colorless crystals.

properties.summary: The cluster shows Eu(III) red emission in the solid state and in dichloromethane. Its emission is quenched by nitrobenzene, with visible quenching at 40 ppm; the authors report predominantly static quenching at low nitrobenzene concentrations.

measurements.name: Nitrobenzene detection limit
measurements.conditions: Luminescence quenching in CH2Cl2; also reported as 85.4 nM

measurements.name: Stern–Volmer quenching constant
measurements.conditions: Nitrobenzene in CH2Cl2; low-concentration linear fit

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The [Eu2Ti4O6]10+ core consists of two triangular EuTi2(μ3-O) units connected by two additional μ3-O bridges and two μ2-O bridges. Its six metal ions form an elongated octahedron, with four Ti ions in equatorial positions and two Eu ions at the apices. Two chelating phen ligands and ten tbza ligands complete the discrete cluster; four acetonitrile molecules occur as guests.
